body: **Foco:** Future Perfect Continuous — produção e revisão.
**Pronúncia:** Ênfase intencional.
**22 palavras novas** (negociações).
**Texto do dia:** conto e trecho de peça.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo produzir um trecho de peça com o Future Perfect Continuous e revisar seu uso e suas armadilhas.

body: Esta aula treina **ler textos curtos e achar informação (IELTS Reading, TOEFL Reading)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

frames.title: Reading · A scene from a play

blocks.title: Scene: The Last Offer
paras: (A conference room. Midnight. IRIS and TOM face each other.)
IRIS: By dawn we **will have been arguing** for fourteen hours, Tom.
TOM: And by then your team **will have been refusing** the same clause for two days. (He sighs.) **Will** you **have been sleeping** at all?
IRIS: Not if we keep this up. But if you drop the penalty, we **will have finished** before breakfast.
TOM: (after a pause) Fine. By the time the sun rises, I **will have been wrong** about one thing: you were never bluffing.

items.q: Iris and Tom have been arguing for hours.
Tom admits Iris was not bluffing.

head: Situação
Forma correta
rows: By dawn we **will have been arguing** for fourteen hours.
By then I **will have known** her for years (não *been knowing*).

blocks.body: Pergunte: **duração (FPC)** ou **resultado (Future Perfect)**? Estado → forma simples.
Evite o FPC quando há **número de vezes** ou **resultado**: *will have read three books*, não *will have been reading three books*.

items.s: By dawn we ___ for fourteen hours. (argue, FPC)
By then I ___ her for years. (know)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.pt: Bom. Agora a resposta de Tom.

items.ans: Say the line again with more tiredness
items.pt: Diga a fala de novo, com mais cansaço.

body: **Call someone’s bluff.** — Pagar para ver o blefe.
**The ball is in your court.** — A bola está com você.
**Break the deadlock.** — Romper o impasse.
**Stick to one’s guns.** — Manter-se firme.
**Dig in one’s heels.** — Fincar o pé.
**Give ground.** — Ceder terreno.
**At a stalemate.** — Em impasse.
**Back to square one.** — De volta à estaca zero.
**Burn the midnight oil.** — Trabalhar noite adentro.
**Say the line again, with more tiredness.** — Diga a fala de novo, com mais cansaço.
**Good. Now Tom’s answer.** — Bom. Agora a resposta de Tom.
**By dawn we will have been arguing for fourteen hours.** — Ao amanhecer estaremos discutindo há catorze horas.

blocks.title: Backstage
lines: Say the line again, with more tiredness.
Diga a fala de novo, com mais cansaço.

items.label: Ênfase intencional
items.note: Pausas e ritmo: faça uma pausa curta entre grupos de sentido (thought groups) e acelere as palavras fracas entre os acentos.
words: If we agree, | we can sign today.
The offer, | as it stands, | is unacceptable.
By Friday | we will have been talking | for a week.

prompts.q: Say how long you will have been living where you live by 2030.
prompts.model: By 2030 I will have been living here for fifteen years.
Will you have been waiting long?
I will have been writing all day; I will have written ten pages.

blocks.task: Write a short two-person scene (6 lines) using the Future Perfect Continuous twice.
blocks.model: A: By noon we will have been waiting for six hours. B: And by then the agent will have been ignoring our calls for two days. A: Will they have been sleeping all week? B: No, but we will have finished the report. A: Then the delay is over. B: Let’s hope so.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
